subject: Frostline security questionnaire: data lifespan & deletion for hosted API
messages:
From: Elena Gomez <elena.gomez@frostline.com>
To: marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Cc: security@frostline.com
Date: 2028-03-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Data lifecycle questions for Frostline hosted integration

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the demo last week — Frostline's security team has a couple of follow-ups for our procurement questionnaire about the hosted API. Can you confirm the following by EOD Friday so we can progress the security review?

1) Where does customer request/response content reside (region and storage type)?
2) Default retention periods for: conversational logs, embeddings, model cache/KV, operational logs/metrics, and backups/snapshots.
3) Deletion process: if we request a full tenant purge, what are the steps and expected timelines? Is there an auditable erasure confirmation we can include in our security pack?
4) Are backups or snapshots stored outside the primary region or replicated cross-region by default?

I've attached our security questionnaire (Frostline_Security_Questionnaire.docx) — I highlighted the data residency/retention block. If you'd prefer a short call to run through answers, we can do that as well.

Best,
Elena
Elena Gomez
Head of Security Programs
Frostline Systems
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Gomez <elena.gomez@frostline.com>
Cc: priyom.das@redwood.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-03-01T13:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Data lifecycle questions for Frostline hosted integration

Hi Elena — thanks for the clear list. Answers below address the hosted API defaults; we can discuss tighter controls in a contract (reserved capacity / private deployment) if you need region lock or shorter backups.

1) Residency and storage
- Primary region: customer requests are served out of the region selected at account creation; for Frostline your account is provisioned in us-west-2 (Oregon).
- Storage types: request/response payloads are stored in encrypted object storage (S3 AES-256) for short-term troubleshooting and telemetry. Model weights are loaded on GPU hosts and not persisted to object storage as part of per-request payloads.

2) Default retention windows (hosted API)
- Conversational logs (request + response bodies): 30 days by default. This window is used for debugging, abuse monitoring, and regression detection.
- Embeddings and derived vectors: 90 days by default unless explicitly stored by the customer in their own downstream storage.
- Inference runtime KV / cache (GPU node caches, prefix KV): ephemeral — typically evicted within 24 hours; never written to long-term object storage as cache by default.
- Operational logs/metrics (aggregated traces, anonymized slices): 180 days for observability; detailed request traces containing payloads follow the 30-day conversation window.
- Backups / snapshots (control-plane and critical metadata): encrypted snapshots retained for 90 days. Snapshots are used for recovery and are strictly access-controlled.

3) Deletion / purge process
- Self-service: For account-level deletion we offer a self-serve request that queues a tenant purge job.
- Timeline: purge is initiated immediately; object storage lifecycle triggers scrub jobs which complete within 72 hours for live request bodies. Backups/snapshots are scheduled for deletion at their next retention cycle and are removed within 7 days of purge initiation (90-day snapshot TTL still applies for historical recovery windows unless explicitly requested for expedited destroy).
- Evidence: after completion we provide an erasure confirmation token (erase-job-id) and an exportable log entry with timestamp and operator id to include in your audit pack.

4) Cross-region replication
- By default the hosted API does not replicate customer request/response payloads to other regions. Control-plane metadata replication uses encrypted channels for high availability but payloads remain in the accounts primary region. Cross-region replication can be enabled under enterprise agreements.

Additional notes:
- Data encryption: at-rest (AES-256) and in-transit (TLS1.2+). Keys are managed in our KMS; for enterprise plans you can supply an external KMS.
- Access controls: production systems that may touch payloads are restricted to a small, audited operator group; access is logged and reviewed.

Attachments: I'm sharing our data lifecycle diagram (redwood-data-lifecycle-diagram.svg) and will attach a short evidence checklist if helpful.

If you want, we can add specific SLAs in the MSA around snapshot retention and immediate snapshot destruction.

—
Marissa Cole
Senior Security Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Elena Gomez <elena.gomez@frostline.com>
To: marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Cc: security@frostline.com
Date: 2028-03-02T10:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Data lifecycle questions for Frostline hosted integration

Thanks Marissa — very helpful. Two quick follow-ups:

A) For the 30-day conversational logs default, can you confirm whether logs are accessible to Redwood support/ops during that window, and what justification is required for access?
B) We need to include a control in our pack that backups won't be moved to another legal jurisdiction without notice. Can you provide language we can use?

Also: do you have an SOC 2 attestation or a link to your compliance folder we can reference in our vendor risk assessment?

Appreciate it,
Elena
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Gomez <elena.gomez@frostline.com>, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Cc: priyom.das@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-03-03T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Data lifecycle questions for Frostline hosted integration

Hi Elena — jumping in to add the requested clarifications and references.

A) Support/ops access to conversational logs:
- Access policy: Support and operations require a documented justification for access (ticket ID + business reason). Access is two-person approved for payload-level inspection. All accesses generate a time-stamped audit record with the requester, approver, purpose, and duration.
- Read-only bundles: When support needs to reproduce an issue we provide ephemeral, access-limited bundles. Those bundles expire after the session and are purged automatically.

B) Suggested vendor pack language re: backup relocation:
- "Redwood Inference will not replicate customer request/response payloads or backups to another legal jurisdiction without prior written notice and consent from the customer. In the event Redwood needs to perform cross-region replication for operational reasons, Redwood will notify the customer at least 30 days in advance and provide options for data residency controls or expedited deletion. Exceptions for legal process will be handled as required by law and communicated per Redwood's incident and legal disclosure policies."

Compliance artifacts: we have a current SOC 2 Type II report and an encrypt-in-transit/at-rest attestation. I'll share a read-only link to the compliance folder once you sign the standard NDA.

Attached for your pack: redwood-data-lifecycle-diagram.svg (diagram) and a short checklist of erasure evidence items.

Let me know if you'd like these answers inserted directly into the Frostline_Security_Questionnaire.docx and returned.

Thanks,
Ben
Ben Carter
Head of Trust & Safety
Redwood Inference
